newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi says still open to early budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi says still open to early budget.

text.p: Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said on Thursday he was still open to talks on shaping an early 1998 budget if Italy's government decided to bring forward the package.

Berlusconi was speaking after several government politicians said on Wednesday that the centre-left coalition had not yet decided whether to bring forward the package or draw up a mini-budget for 1997.
"I know for certain that the state accounts are going badly," Berlusconi told Reuters in parliament.
"I don't understand how they (the government) can manage not to think about a mini-budget and to think about the next budget as if it were just any budget," he said.
"If the government has second thoughts, we are always here and will show a sense of responsibility," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi said last month he would like to bring forward passage of the 1998 budget by several months to send a signal to Italy's European Union partners that it was serious about reforming state finances in time for planned monetary union.
He has also said he will draw up a mini-budget for 1997 if state accounts, to be published early next month, on the 1996 deficit show supplementary deficit-cutting measures are necessary.
Government politicians on Wednesday, however, said the issues were still being reviewed.
They said there were two options including a mini-budget and a 1998 budget on normal schedule or just an early 1998 budget. They said a decision would be made once the accounts were published.
